The item directly assesses Topic 9.2 (The Ideal Gas Law), which explicitly states that 'the temperature at which an ideal gas would have zero pressure can be extrapolated from a P-vs-T graph.' The mathematics is completely consistent: with slope m = (160 - 120)/(127 - 27) = 0.4 kPa/°C, setting P = 0 yields T = 27 - (120 / 0.4) = -273°C (absolute zero).

The item tests the ideal gas law at constant volume and the extrapolation of a pressure-versus-temperature graph to zero pressure, both explicitly addressed in Unit 9.2 of the CED fact pack: 'Graphs of P, T, V can describe/determine gas properties; the temperature at which an ideal gas would have zero pressure can be extrapolated from a P-vs-T graph.' The given data are internally consistent with a constant-volume ideal gas (120 kPa at 300 K and 160 kPa at 400 K, both giving P/T = 0.4 kPa/K), and the straight-line extrapolation correctly yields approximately −273°C. The Celsius-to-Kelvin conversion is a standard mathematical step required for using the ideal gas law and is not excluded by any boundary statement. No out-of-scope concepts or exclusions apply.
